recent_posts.title: Announcing the AI Gateway Working Group
recent_posts.summary: The Kubernetes community has formed the AI Gateway Working Group (WG AI Gateway), a new initiative to develop standards and best practices for networking infrastructure supporting AI workloads. An AI Gateway in Kubernetes context refers to network infrastructure implementing the Gateway API with AI-specific capabilities like token-based rate limiting, fine-grained access controls, payload inspection, and AI-protocol routing. Active proposals include payload processing (covering security features like prompt injection protection and optimization features like semantic routing and caching) and egress gateways (for securely routing traffic to external AI services like OpenAI, Vertex AI, and Bedrock). The group is presenting at KubeCon Europe 2026 in Amsterdam and welcomes contributions from gateway implementers, platform operators, and AI developers via GitHub, weekly meetings, and Slack.

recent_posts.title: Spotlight on SIG Architecture: API Governance
recent_posts.summary: Jordan Liggitt, lead of Kubernetes SIG Architecture's API Governance subproject, discusses how the team maintains stability and consistency across all Kubernetes APIs while enabling innovation. The subproject reviews API changes at design or implementation stages, enforces conventions through guidelines and automated tools, and ensures conceptual integrity. Custom Resource Definitions marked a watershed moment, shifting from fully controlled APIs to user-defined ones, requiring new validation capabilities. API Governance balances backward compatibility promises with evolution, assuming future knowledge will require design flexibility while protecting users from breaking changes.

recent_posts.title: Announcing the Checkpoint/Restore Working Group
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes announces a new Checkpoint/Restore Working Group focused on integrating checkpoint/restore functionality into Kubernetes. The group addresses use cases including optimizing resource utilization for interactive workloads, accelerating startup times for applications with long initialization, enabling fault-tolerance through periodic checkpointing, supporting interruption-aware scheduling, facilitating pod migration, and enabling forensic analysis. The working group bridges the Kubernetes community with the CRIU ecosystem, which includes tools like CRIU, checkpointctl, criu-coordinator, and checkpoint-restore-operator. Contributors can participate through bi-weekly meetings, Slack channels, and mailing lists.

recent_posts.title: Ingress NGINX Retirement: What You Need to Know
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes SIG Network and Security Response Committee are retiring Ingress NGINX, one of the most popular Ingress controllers. Best-effort maintenance continues until March 2026, after which no updates, bugfixes, or security patches will be provided. The retirement stems from insufficient maintainership and mounting technical debt. Existing deployments will continue functioning and artifacts remain available, but users are strongly advised to migrate immediately to Gateway API or alternative Ingress controllers. The project's repositories will become read-only for reference.

recent_posts.title: Announcing the 2025 Steering Committee Election Results
recent_posts.summary: The Kubernetes Steering Committee announced its 2025 election results, with four new members elected to two-year terms: Kat Cosgrove (Minimus), Paco Xu (DaoCloud), Rita Zhang (Microsoft), and Maciej Szulik (Defense Unicorns). They join three continuing members from Google and Red Hat. The Steering Committee oversees governance for the entire Kubernetes project and holds open monthly meetings where community members can participate.

recent_posts.title: Spotlight on Policy Working Group
recent_posts.summary: The Kubernetes Policy Working Group, now completed, focused on standardizing policy management across the Kubernetes ecosystem. The group developed the Policy Reports API, created whitepapers on policy management and compliance, updated Kubernetes documentation, and worked to educate the community on best practices. Key accomplishments included standardizing policy reporting across tools like Falco, Trivy, and Kyverno, and providing guidance on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy. The group collaborated closely with SIG Auth and SIG Security, operating as a temporary, cross-cutting initiative distinct from permanent Special Interest Groups.

recent_posts.title: Spotlight on the Kubernetes Steering Committee
recent_posts.summary: Five current Kubernetes Steering Committee members share insights about their roles, responsibilities, and experiences leading one of the world's largest open source projects. They discuss how the committee handles organizational challenges, supports contributors, and maintains project governance while delegating technical work to Special Interest Groups. The interview covers their motivations for joining, favorite aspects of the role, challenges like contributor sustainability, and advice for future candidates.

recent_posts.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography in Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes v1.33 now supports post-quantum cryptography by default through Go 1.24's implementation of X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange. This quantum-resistant encryption protects against future quantum computer attacks on current cryptographic standards. While key exchange mechanisms are ready, post-quantum digital signatures face challenges with larger key sizes and performance overhead. The transition includes potential pitfalls like Go version mismatches causing downgrades to classical cryptography and packet size issues with ClientHello messages.

recent_posts.title: Changes to Kubernetes Slack
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes community's Slack workspace will lose its free enterprise status on June 20, 2025, reverting to a standard free plan with limitations like 90-day message history retention. The CNCF is considering migrating to Discord as an alternative platform that could offer better integrations and tools for the large community. Channel owners and user group members need to take immediate action to preserve important information before the transition.

recent_posts.title: Spotlight on SIG Apps
recent_posts.summary: SIG Apps is a Special Interest Group within the Kubernetes community that focuses on developing, deploying, and operating applications on Kubernetes. Leaders Maciej Szulik and Janet Kuo discuss their roles, significant initiatives such as AI/ML workload support, best practices for application management, and how new contributors can get involved. They emphasize challenges like rejecting feature suggestions and the importance of community feedback and participation.
